stated_availability: Data availability statement (p. 8): "Supplementary Information to this article can be found online at https://zenodo.org/records/10801706." Methods §2.2 (p. 3): "Dedicated R code and complete data tables are reported in Supplementary Information S2 and S3. All analyses were performed in the open-source R programming environment (v.4.2.2; R Core Team, 2021), using the Quanteda package (Benoit et al., 2018). All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550." Appendix A (p. 8): "Supplementary data to this article can be found online at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jas.2024.105969." Descriptive record only; no L1-L6 level assigned (L-levels are assigned at reproduction time per preregistration §7.3).

F1.evidence: "All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550" (p. 3) and "Supplementary Information to this article can be found online at https://zenodo.org/records/10801706" (Data availability statement, p. 8). Zenodo is an archival, DOI-minting repository (every published record carries a DataCite DOI and a globally unique record accession); supplementary data also reachable via the article DOI ("Supplementary data to this article can be found online at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jas.2024.105969", Appendix A). Note: the paper cites the Zenodo record URLs rather than the 10.5281/zenodo.* DOI form.

F2.evidence: Deposit in Zenodo (records 10623550, 10801706), which structurally enforces DataCite-structured metadata (creators, title, description, resource type) on every published record; reference-guide precedent awards F2 for Zenodo deposits ("Zenodo generates DataCite metadata automatically").

F3.evidence: Zenodo/DataCite metadata mandatorily includes the record's identifier (DOI) as a required field; structural consequence of the evidenced Zenodo deposit (records 10623550, 10801706).

F4.evidence: Deposited in Zenodo, explicitly listed in the instrument's F4 examples of searchable registries; Zenodo records are indexed via DataCite/OpenAIRE.

A1.evidence: Full research dataset retrievable via standard HTTPS: "All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550" (p. 3). Coverage is complete - the deposited S1 corpus covers all 483 analysed objects ("With a total of 483 objects (Supplementary Information S1)", p. 2) plus complete data tables (S3), so the A1 completeness rule does not trigger.

A1_1.evidence: Zenodo records and the journal supplement are served over open, free HTTPS with no registration, subscription, or proprietary protocol required; article is open access.

A1_2.evidence: The protocol in use (HTTPS via Zenodo) supports authentication/authorisation where needed (Zenodo provides restricted/embargoed access mechanisms); no restriction is needed for this non-sensitive published-catalogue data and none is imposed.

A2.evidence: Zenodo commits to long-term metadata persistence via DataCite registration (CERN-operated, 20+ year preservation commitment); metadata persists even if files are removed. Structural property of the evidenced deposit.

I1.evidence: Structured, machine-readable tabular data: motifs "transcribed as binary data in the form of presence/absence coding of motif types (named A1, A2, etc.)" then "transformed from presence/absence coding into a sentence-imitating structure" (p. 2), and processed directly by the deposited R/quanteda code - a formal, shared representation.

I2.evidence: Motif vocabulary follows "Plonka's (2003, pp. 315-325) own motif classification scheme, the most comprehensive for Mesolithic portable art" (p. 2) - a print-monograph classification with no PIDs, URIs, or machine-readable form; no FAIR vocabulary evidenced.

I3.evidence: No evidence that the dataset's metadata includes typed PID references to other resources; the upstream source (Plonka 2003 monograph) has no PID, and Zenodo related-identifier links cannot be evidenced from the paper alone.

R1.evidence: "These data consist of numerous categorical variables corresponding to the characteristics of each ornamented object and associated metadata such as location, quality of contextual information, and original source" (p. 2) - a plurality of relevant attributes, with detailed description of coding and transformation in Methods.

R1_1.evidence: Article and its supplementary information published under "the CC BY license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)" (p. 1); Zenodo additionally mandates a licence field on every published open record (reference-guide precedent: "licence captured in Zenodo metadata").

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance: "From this analogue compilation, the South Scandinavian data were manually extracted and digitised" from Plonka (2003), with the presence/absence-to-sentence transformation documented (p. 2); software versions stated (R v4.2.2, quanteda); CRediT names Herskind for "Data curation" (p. 8).

R1_3.evidence: No domain-relevant community data standard evidenced (no ARIADNEplus, CIDOC-CRM, Dublin Core, or similar); Plonka's motif scheme is a single-monograph classification, not a formal community data/metadata standard.

F1.evidence: "Dedicated R code and complete data tables are reported in Supplementary Information S2 and S3... All code and data are available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550" (p. 3). Zenodo is an archival, DOI-minting repository; the record accession is globally unique and persistent. Note: cited as record URL, not DOI form.

F2.evidence: Code deposited in Zenodo record 10623550, which structurally enforces DataCite-structured metadata (creators, title, description, resource type) on every published record.

F3.evidence: Zenodo/DataCite metadata mandatorily includes the record's identifier (DOI); structural consequence of the evidenced Zenodo deposit.

F4.evidence: Deposited in Zenodo, explicitly listed in the instrument's F4 examples of searchable registries; indexed via DataCite/OpenAIRE.

A1.evidence: Complete analysis code ("Dedicated R code", S2, covering "All analyses") retrievable via standard HTTPS from Zenodo record 10623550 and via the journal supplement at the article DOI.

A1_1.evidence: Open, free HTTPS access with no registration or proprietary protocol; the code targets the "open-source R programming environment" (p. 3).

A1_2.evidence: HTTPS via Zenodo supports authentication/authorisation where needed (Zenodo restricted-access mechanisms exist); no restriction needed for this code and none imposed.

A2.evidence: Zenodo commits to long-term metadata persistence via DataCite registration; metadata persists even if the resource is removed. Structural property of the evidenced deposit.

I1.evidence: R scripts in an open-source, standard, widely shared language: "All analyses were performed in the open-source R programming environment (v.4.2.2; R Core Team, 2021), using the Quanteda package (Benoit et al., 2018)" (p. 3).

I2.evidence: No evidence of FAIR vocabulary or software metadata standards (no CodeMeta, ontology-based annotation) applied to the code artefact.

I3.evidence: The paper cites dependencies with versions and a DOI (R v4.2.2; quanteda - Benoit et al. 2018, https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.00774 in the reference list), but there is no evidence that the deposited code artefact itself includes qualified, typed PID references to its dependencies.

R1.evidence: Analysis pipeline richly described: skipgram generation with k set to 13 ("the k value for all generated skip-grams is thus set to 13", p. 3), expected-frequency and PMI formulas given in full, environment and package versions stated (R v4.2.2, quanteda), and 2-/3-/4-gram outputs specified.

R1_1.evidence: Article and supplementary materials published under "the CC BY license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)" (p. 1); Zenodo mandates a licence field on every published open record (reference-guide precedent for Zenodo-archived code).

R1_2.evidence: Provenance documented: software versions (R v4.2.2, quanteda), analysis parameters (k = 13; 2-, 3-, 4-grams), and workflow order described in Methods (pp. 2-3); CRediT statement assigns Formal analysis and Methodology roles (p. 8).

R1_3.evidence: No evidence of software community standards for the deposited scripts (no CRAN packaging, CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, containerisation, or environment lock file).

barriers: Upstream analogue source (Plonka 2003, The Portable Art of Mesolithic Europe, Wydawnictwo Uniwersytetu Wroclawskiego) is a printed monograph requiring library or purchase access (Tier 2); however, the complete digitised corpus of all 483 analysed objects (S1) and the complete derived data tables (S3) are deposited at Tier 0 (Zenodo records 10623550 and 10801706, plus the journal supplement via the article DOI), so no reproduction-relevant data barrier remains. Record-weighted coverage of analysed objects: 483/483 = 100%.
